conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that scientific evidence indicates widespread mask wearing can reduce COVID-19 infections and high population adoption effectively reduces community transmission.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion**
Scientific evidence indicates that widespread mask wearing **can** reduce COVID-19 infections, though real-world impact depends on compliance and mask usage.

**Key Evidence**
* **Large Cluster-Randomized Trial:** A trial involving over 340,000 adults across 600 villages in Bangladesh demonstrated that community-level mask promotion increased mask wearing and significantly reduced symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections (https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.abi9069).
* **Population Evidence Review:** An interdisciplinary review in *PNAS* evaluated community transmission data and concluded that widespread use of face masks reduces SARS-CoV-2 transmission (https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2014564118).
* **Systematic Review Considerations:** A Cochrane review evaluated trial evidence on physical interventions for respiratory viruses (https://www.cochrane.org/about-us/news/featured-review-physical-interventions-interrupt-or-reduce-spread-respiratory-viruses). While systematic reviews note variable findings across trials—often due to differing adherence rates—large-scale studies confirm that increasing actual community mask usage lowers infection rates.

Overall, evidence shows that high mask adoption across a population effectively reduces community transmission.

**Sources:**
* https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.abi9069
* https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2014564118
* https://www.cochrane.org/about-us/news/featured-review-physical-interventions-interrupt-or-reduce-spread-respiratory-viruses
